closure_audit.negative_recall_original_abstract: Ongoing climate warming is thawing global permafrost, making vast pools of organic carbon available as microbial growth substrates. This ecological disturbance should be readily observable as a functional shift within microbial communities. Thus, permafrost thaw not only motivates, but also serves as a promising testing ground for the development of metagenomic tools that can assess the competitive abilities of individual taxa in complex, mixed-species communities. Here we develop and validate a genomic index of copiotrophy that predicts early microbial success post-thaw in permafrost soils, compare the behavior of this index across environments including diverse soils, the open ocean, and the human microbiome, and implement this index in an R package that enables users to fit their own system-specific index of copiotrophy.
